stories.description: El ejemplar padece xantocromismo, una condición poco frecuente que provoca una coloración amarillo-anaranjada.
stories.excerpt: El ejemplar padece xantocromismo, una condición poco frecuente que provoca una coloración amarillo-anaranjada. Un ejemplar de lota (Lota lota) con una llamativa coloración amarilla ha sido capturado en el lago Oswego, en el estado de Nueva York (Estados Unidos). El hallazgo ha sorprendido a los científicos por tratarse de un fenómeno excepcional en esta especie, cuyos individuos suelen presentar tonos marrones oscuros moteados, negros o grises. Los expertos han calificado al pez como un ejemplar singular “uno entre un millón”. La peculiar apariencia del animal se debe al xantocromismo, una alteración biológica poco común relacionada con una mutación genética que modifica la pigmentación habitual y produce tonalidades amarillas o anaranjadas intensas. Según explica el Servicio de Pesca y Vida Silvestre de Estados Unidos (USFWS), esta condición es mucho menos frecuente en peces salvajes que el albinismo o el melanismo, lo que hace especialmente inusual el descubrimiento. The film evokes a sense of déjà vu, an inescapable loophole in time and space. Since last week's trilateral Russia-Ukraine-U.S. talks in Abu Dhabi, the reports about Russian demands appearing in the media have given me the same feeling of entrapment, the same sense of déjà vu. stories.title: 26 Greenlanders sue Denmark over denial of paternity, inheritance rights
stories.description: Plaintiffs each seek $18,400 in compensation over former rules affecting children born outside marriage
stories.excerpt: A trial opened Tuesday at Denmark’s Eastern High Court in a compensation case brought by 26 Greenlanders who were denied the right to have their fathers legally recognized and to inherit from them, Danish public broadcaster DR reported. The plaintiffs are each seeking 125,000 Danish kroner ($18,400) from the Danish state, arguing that the rules in force when they were born denied them the same rights as Greenlandic children born to married parents. Children born outside marriage in Denmark had rights that their Greenlandic counterparts were denied. The plaintiffs are among a group known as the “legally fatherless.” The Greenland Children’s Act took effect in West Greenland in 1963 and in North and East Greenland in 1974. Up to 5,000 Greenlanders alive today may have been affected by the earlier rules, according to the report.
